executiveConclusion: The requested A3-A6 ramp and 300 s fixed hold diagnostic is complete locally under an explicit conservative one-way gate-face assumption. The outward ramp path is the bound legacy path; the hold from model time 300 to 600 used the copied one-way kernel at A3-A6 100% capacity and completed 36,634 accepted steps with maximum CFL 0.12, relative mass error 9.12e-15, full 28,746-cell limiter coverage, and zero negative/nonfinite state or fishway flow. However, the operator blocked potential reverse flow on 34,923 steps with 7,415 m3 cumulative potential reverse volume and up to all 29 active A3-A6 faces at once. The result is therefore a numerical diagnostic dominated by the imposed one-way assumption, not physical validation. YODA repetition would add cost without changing this gate; do not promote to forecast, GUI fishing guidance, mesh adoption, or release.

remoteYodaReceipt.failure: adverse barrage discharge detected; result rejected without clipping

mainFindings.finding: A3-A6 fixed ramp/hold is both fail-closed numerically and outside the published 24-270 m3/s regulating-gate operation for the bound 38 m3/s forcing.

A8-only 25, 50, 75, and 100 percent local cases each held 600 s with zero negative/nonfinite states, no interlock, and no local adverse volume under gate-weighted head and gate-net outward-flux checks.

The official micro-adjustment gate is a separate 10 m by 2.8 m oil-hydraulic tilting gate and should be fully open in the bound operation band, but its physical discharge law is not available in the reviewed public sources.
A pure equal-and-opposite transfer primitive is ready for an externally authorised outward discharge; it does not infer discharge from width and is not connected to the solver.

The pure transfer primitive was wired at exactly Q=0 to the 28,746-cell regularized context; all sources remained zero and the existing one-step state and scalar results remained bit-identical. Nonzero connection remains forbidden.

After correcting the donor mask to the 56 positive P2 overlap cells, local Q commands 0, 6, 12, 18, and 24 m3/s each completed 60 s with zero negative/nonfinite states and conservative mass. Every nonzero command generated an adverse head and was smoothly self-limited; average effective Q was only 0.90-1.04 m3/s. This is a coupling safety result, not a gate rating.

The first nonzero-Q implementation incorrectly used the entire upstream component as the donor support. That result was discarded; the canonical implementation and report use only positive P2 donor-overlap cells.

The common-state 3-by-3 sparse matrix completed without negative or nonfinite values. A8 50 percent held for all Q but accumulated 0.528-0.539 m3 of local adverse face exchange. A8 100 percent tripped at 21.298 s for all Q. Micro Q changed neither outcome materially, so A8 observation and local flux behavior dominate the blocker.

The existing 600 s real-context A3-A6 probe completed numerically, but one adverse face appeared on A6, A5, A3, and A4 at 314.317, 322.796, 340.032, and 341.766 model seconds. Each affected gate still had positive integrated discharge, proving that a gate sum can hide forbidden local reverse flow; all four gates latched closed.

At the already-adverse first-trip state, exact tentative post-step trials at a common 0.00838593 s dt rejected 100% and found that an 87.5% trial ended with all 29 active faces outward. Because its pre-step state was already adverse, this is recovery evidence only and cannot be accepted as a strict-one-way transition.

Starting at model time 300 s, the preventive controller required every accepted candidate to be facewise safe both before and after the step. It completed 60 s with positive minimum accepted pre/post face flux, no negative/nonfinite state, and no fishway flow, but made eight monotonic decreases and reached zero opening at 336.322 s. Reopening probes at 346.318 and 356.325 s rejected 12.5% because all 29 faces were adverse. Numerical safety passed; nonzero hold utility failed.

A pure face-branch operator now selects the existing open-interface/wall blend for outward flow and two reflected-wall terms for adverse flow. Synthetic tests require equal-and-opposite mass terms, zero wall mass, SHA-bound upstream orientation, no post-hoc state repair, and explicit structure momentum reaction. It is not connected to the numerical kernel and is not physical validation.

A copied local kernel entrypoint applies the one-way branch without modifying the legacy kernel. On the 28,746-cell real context, the outward mid-ramp case is bit-exact to the legacy state, scalars, and limiter. A +0.30 m adverse downstream perturbation blocks 29 faces, reports 17.9325 m3/s potential reverse discharge, preserves global mass with zero measured relative error, scans 28,746/28,746 limiter candidates, and produces no negative/nonfinite state or fishway flow. This is one-step numerical evidence, not duration or physical validation.

The bounded 300-to-360 s fixed A3-A6 hold completed 7,180 steps at 100% capacity with numerical safety and mass conservation. The one-way branch was active on 5,469 steps and blocked 197.014 m3 cumulative potential reverse volume, showing that the assumption is already material during the short canary.

The full 300-to-600 s hold completed locally in 70.47 wall seconds with 36,634 accepted steps, maximum CFL 0.12, mass error 9.12e-15, no negative/nonfinite state, zero fishway flow, and full limiter coverage. The one-way branch was active on 34,923 steps, blocked 867,158 face-step observations and 7,415.119 m3 cumulative potential reverse volume, and reached all 29 active faces. This passes the numerical diagnostic only and fails any claim that the one-way assumption is a negligible correction.

recommendedNextDecision.question: What evidence is required before the one-way 300 s diagnostic can influence the simulator or fishing GUI?
recommendedNextDecision.optionA: Obtain or define an engineering one-way discharge and momentum law for the actual barrage and validate it against observed upstream/downstream levels and gate operation before connecting the candidate kernel to forecasts.
recommendedNextDecision.optionB: Use the symmetric hydraulic model and allow the operational controller to close the gates; this is numerically conservative but does not provide the requested nonzero Stage-4 hold.
recommendedNextDecision.optionC: Retain the current one-way wall branch only as a sensitivity bound showing the maximum effect of forbidding reverse exchange, with the 7,415 m3 blocked potential volume displayed as a model-dependence warning.
recommendedNextDecision.whyAIsRecommended: The full hold is numerically stable, but the one-way branch is active for most of the hold and blocks a large potential exchange volume. Repeating it on YODA does not validate the gate law. Observational or engineering calibration is now the limiting evidence, not compute time.
recommendedNextDecision.nextLocalWorkAfterDecision: Stop numerical expansion. Preserve the local diagnostic and prepare a concise model-assumption/validation checklist. Do not update forecast products, fishing suitability, or GUI layers until the one-way gate law is externally justified.
